data.why: the repo ships no example plate photos and the README says a researcher supplies their own, so two small Netpbm-PGM grayscale images (named .jpg so Streamlit's file-type filter accepts them; OpenCV decodes by content signature, not extension) were authored: one with four distinct square 'colonies' of varying size including one touching the image border, and one blank plate with zero colonies as a negative-control edge case.

goals: Upload a photo of an agar plate and get an automated colony count
Adjust the detection confidence threshold slider to see how it changes the number of detected colonies
Visually verify detections by inspecting the bounding boxes overlaid on the plate image
Switch to Identify mode to see colonies broken out by detected class/species with a color legend
Confirm the tool correctly reports zero colonies on a blank/negative-control plate

review.summary: The tree matches what the README and the code say the tool is for: automated colony counting, plus species identification, with a confidence cutoff and boxes drawn on the image. Every cited screen I opened supports its node, and the not_done notes are honest. It needs light fixes before filing: merge the overlapping cutoff tasks, recast the Streamlit Rerun as a consistency check, and record the swatch/box colour mismatch as a confirmed RGB/BGR bug instead of a one-off.
